program_name: FERC Order 2222 implementation status - DER Participation Model
incentive_structure: Rule / timeline row - no direct payment
event_limits: Timeline: NYISO filed its Aggregation participation model June 27 2019 (Docket ER19-2276); FERC accepted it January 23 2020 (170 FERC 61033). NYISO filed its Order 2222 compliance filing July 19 2021; FERC accepted it June 17 2022 while directing 30+ further tariff modifications. FERC granted NYISO an extension to December 31 2026 to complete full Order 2222 compliance. NYISO filed further DER tariff revisions June 1 2023 (Docket ER23-2040); FERC accepted them April 15 2024 (187 FERC 61022) and expressly found the 10 kW minimum capability requirement just and reasonable and NOT a temporary measure, while directing an informational report which NYISO filed April 15 2026. The DER and Aggregation participation model is LIVE today under the interim (pre-Order-2222) rules; dual-participation, operating-reserve composition and other rules change when the Order 2222-compliant tariff takes effect
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 through 4.1.10.7.3; FERC Docket Nos. ER19-2276, ER21-2460, ER23-2040

program_name: Small Utility opt-in gate for DER Aggregation participation
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
event_limits: New York has NO statewide opt-out of third-party aggregation of retail customers. The only gate is the Order 2222 small-utility provision: a Resource that is a customer of a Small Utility may not be enrolled in an Aggregation unless the Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority affirmatively authorizes (opts in to) such participation. NYISO defines Small Utility as a Distribution Utility that distributed four million MWh or less in NYISO's immediately prior completed fiscal year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). The determination applies for the forthcoming Capability Year. If a RERRA later withdraws authorization and the Aggregator notifies NYISO before April 1, the DER is ineligible from the first day of the following Capability Year; if notice comes on or after April 1 but before May 1, the DER is ineligible as of June 1
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 4.1.10 (definitions of Distribution Utility and Small Utility)
stackable_with: Customers of New York's large investor-owned distribution utilities (over 4 million MWh/yr) face no opt-in gate and may join an Aggregation directly

program_name: Prohibition on duplicative compensation - same service in wholesale and retail
incentive_structure: Stacking gate - no payment
event_limits: A DER may not provide the SAME service in the NYISO-administered markets that it already provides in a retail service or program. FERC struck NYISO's originally proposed broader phrase or substantially similar as an improperly broad restriction, so the bar is same service only. The Aggregator must attest at enrollment that DER enrolled in its Aggregation are not providing the same service in a retail service or program, and must attest to compliance with the Distribution Utilities' tariffs and the RERRA's rules

VDER Environmental Value (REC), Demand Reduction Value (DRV), Locational System Relief Value (LSRV), Market Transition Credit, Community Credit and Non-Mass Market Community Credit ARE stackable with a NYISO DER Aggregation. For storage, DRV, LSRV, MTC and Non-Mass Market Community Credit are stackable. Net Energy Metering is Utility Only and NOT stackable. Customers taking service under a utility Buyback Tariff are not eligible to participate in the NYISO DER aggregation model per tariff. Applicable retail tariffs are WVS and WDS (import and export) for storage; WDS tariffs are not yet approved or filed at FERC for all utilities
tariff_schedule: NY PSC VDER Value Stack; utility WVS and WDS tariffs; NYISO Services Tariff 4.1.10.6

stackable_with: VDER DRV; VDER LSRV; VDER Environmental Value/REC; VDER Market Transition Credit; VDER Community Credit; Non-Wires Alternative contracts

Utility Demand Response Program ENERGY payments are stackable but the resource is ineligible for the utility performance payment in hours with overlapping NYISO energy payments. Non-Wires Alternative contracts are stackable for all resource types including Landfill Gas. Separately, NYISO's own DR programs (SCR and EDRP) are marked fully stackable with utility DR programs during NYISO's interim market

program_name: DER Aggregation - eligibility sizing rules (10 kW DER / 100 kW Aggregation / 20 MW injection cap)
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
event_limits: Minimum capability of each individual DER (including a Demand Side Resource) participating in an Aggregation is 10 kW; where a DER includes multiple assets of different technologies at the facility, EACH asset must independently meet 10 kW. Minimum size of a DER Aggregation is 100 kW; an Aggregation that offers a combination of Energy injections, Energy withdrawals and/or Demand Reduction must be able to offer at least 100 kW of each. Maximum Injection Limit for an injecting facility in an Aggregation is 20 MW; there is no size cap on Demand Reduction resources. All DER in an Aggregation must be on the SAME Transmission Node and therefore in the same NYISO Load Zone. A DER facility has a single point of interconnection and a single utility account number, and may participate in only one Aggregation at a time. FERC found the 10 kW minimum just and reasonable on April 15 2024 and confirmed it is not a temporary measure
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 and 4.1.10.1; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual)
stackable_with: Resources under 10 kW remain eligible for EDRP, the SCR program (including Small Customer Aggregation) and NY State and utility DER programs

program_name: Energy Storage Resource (ESR) and Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) participation models
incentive_structure: Full participation in Energy, Ancillary Services and Installed Capacity markets as a standalone ESR, or as a Single Resource Type Aggregation of ESRs
event_limits: NYISO was the first ISO/RTO to allow full ESR participation in energy, capacity and ancillary services markets, implemented under FERC Order No. 841 (FERC accepted NYISO's Order 841 compliance revisions December 20 2019; full-participation model went live in 2020). Minimum size for wholesale participation as an ESR is 100 kW. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is a regulation-focused model and must bid ISO-Committed-Flexible; an ESR may bid ISO-Committed-Flexible or Self-Committed Fixed/Flexible. Capacity market eligibility extends to resources able to store as little as two hours of energy, with time-stacking applied to resources with an Energy Duration Limitation (EDL). ESRs may withdraw (charge) at retail rates under Services Tariff 7.2.8
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 7.2.8 and 15.4.1.2.4; ICAP Manual Attachment J; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.1.3

stackable_with: Energy arbitrage + Regulation + Operating Reserves + ICAP from the same ESR; ESR-only Single Resource Type Aggregation; heterogeneous DER Aggregation with solar and demand response

Requires 6-second AGC base point following and 6-second two-way telemetry. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is the regulation-oriented storage model and bids ISO-Committed-Flexible. program_name: Operating Reserves (10-Minute Spinning, 10-Minute Non-Synchronized, 30-Minute Synchronized, 30-Minute Non-Synchronized)
incentive_structure: $/MWh marginal clearing price by product and by reserve region
event_limits: Four Operating Reserve products. Under current rules an Aggregation may only offer the product that EVERY member DER can supply - an aggregation of one 10-minute-spin facility plus two 30-minute-non-sync facilities can only offer 30-minute non-synchronized reserve. Aggregations must bid self-committed flexible; self-committed fixed and ISO-committed fixed bid modes are ineligible for reserves. New reserve Aggregations verify performance during the first two weeks of the first active month instead of prequalifying. DSASP resources must follow 5-minute RTD base points. Reserve prices differ by region (NYCA, East, SENY, Long Island); clearing prices not captured here

program_name: Monthly Net Benefit Threshold (MNBT) - Order 745 net benefits test
incentive_structure: Price floor that gates energy payments for Demand Reductions
event_limits: NYISO runs the Net Benefits Test monthly and posts the Monthly Net Benefit Threshold by the 15th of the preceding month on its Demand Response page. A DER Aggregation or DADRP resource may OFFER below the MNBT, but Demand Reductions performed in an interval where the applicable Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT earn no Energy payment, no Day-Ahead Margin Assurance Payment and no Bid Production Cost Guarantee. Exception: if NYISO or the Transmission Owner dispatches the Aggregation for NYCA or local system reliability, the Demand Reductions remain eligible. A DER Aggregation also may not balance Energy withdrawals by Withdrawal-Eligible Generators against Demand Reductions in a Real-Time interval when the Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT. Current monthly values not captured here - they change every month
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.4.1.2, 4.5.2, 4.5.2.1, 4.5.7 and 4.5.7.1; Technical Bulletin 245; NYISO Manual 38 Section 2.1.3.2

RGGI CO2 allowance prices averaged nearly $23/ton in 2025, contributing more than $10/MWh (about 28 percent of production cost) for a typical Central Zone combined cycle

program_name: SCR to DER Participation Model transition rules
incentive_structure: No payment - switching rule between the two capacity-earning DR pathways
event_limits: An active SCR may move to the DER participation model monthly: the SCR must be separated in DRIS before the close of the Certification period for the auction month preceding the intended first DER month. A transitioning SCR may use a Provisional DMNC capped at the upper limit of Installed Capacity calculated for the SCR (its former Average Coincident Load) for the immediately prior like Capability Period, submitted within the first 7 days of the pending-review month; the Provisional DMNC must later be validated by an in-period DMNC test and the Aggregation is exposed to oversold-capacity penalties. Moving the other way is much slower: a DER whose capability contributed to an Aggregation's UCAP must give notice by August 1 and can only rejoin the SCR program the following May 1. An SCR base performance test cannot substitute for a DMNC test. As of June 2025 the MMU reported only ONE demand response resource had actually transitioned from SCR to DER
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.11.1, 5.12.11.1.1 and 5.12.13.1; NYISO Manual 38 Sections 2.2.5 and 4.3.3
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with SCR - a resource cannot be both an SCR and a DER at the same time

program_name: Distributed Energy Resource Provider (DERP) - Distributed Energy Resource Aggregation (DERA), energy and ancillary services
incentive_structure: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LMP at the aggregation's PNode(s) (weighted by Generation Distribution Factors) plus $/MW ancillary service capacity awards; settled as a single supply resource
event_limits: Aggregation minimum 100 kW (reduced from 0.5 MW under Order 2222; validated as aggregate Pmax >= 0.1 MW); individual DERs must be under 1 MW (a generating unit of 1 MW or more in the CAISO BAA must become a Participating Generator instead); aggregation spanning multiple PNodes capped at 20 MW; all DERs must sit in ONE Sub-LAP; a DER may be in only one DERA and may not also participate in the CAISO market separately. Modeled as a generic Non-Generating Resource, non-REM subtype. Requires a DERP Agreement (Tariff Appendix B.21), a certified Scheduling Coordinator with a Meter Service Agreement for SCs (SC Metered Entity, SQMD submitted daily for all intervals), a 30-business-day UDC/MSS concurrence review before New Resource Implementation, and UDC interconnection (Rule 21 / WDT) approval. Telemetry: not required for energy-only unless 10 MW or greater; required at any size for Spin/Non-Spin (4-second status). Aggregated response at each PNode must move in the direction of the dispatch
tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 4.17 (4.17.3 Requirements, 4.17.4 UDC review, 4.17.5 Characteristics, 4.17.6 Operating Requirements) and Appendix B.21 (DERP Agreement); Appendix K ASRP A.1.1/B.1.1/C.1.1; BPM for Generator Management; BPM for Market Instruments; BPM for Direct Telemetry
export_compensation: Net injections settled at PNode LMP (GDF-weighted); charging settled as negative supply
stackable_with: Energy + Spinning + Non-Spinning Reserve from the same DERA. NOT eligible to provide Resource Adequacy per CAISO's PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA comparison matrix (Nov 2023). A DER in a DERA may not also be in another DERA, may not bid separately, and may not be on a retail NEM program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation (Tariff 4.17.3). Seven entities hold DERP Agreements (3rd Rock Systems, Apparent Energy, Galt Power, Olivine, SDG&E, Shell Energy North America, Silicon Valley Clean Energy)

program_name: Heterogeneous DER Aggregation (HDERA) with Distributed Curtailment Resources - FERC Order 2222 model
incentive_structure: $/MWh LMP on the SUM of net DER energy injection plus DCR demand curtailment (curtailment metered as positive supply); settled as one generic NGR non-REM resource
event_limits: Live since November 1 2024 (Tariff 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6). Must contain at least one Distributed Curtailment Resource (demand response) and may also contain injecting DERs. Minimum 100 kW aggregate Pmax. All locations in the same Sub-LAP; PNodes Pre-Defined (default GDFs) or Customized (DERP-specified GDFs summing to 1); GDFs may be resubmitted with hourly bids. Bids are subject to the same Net Benefits Test price threshold as PDR. DCR curtailment is measured against an ISO-approved baseline from Tariff 4.13.4 (weather matching, control group, day-matching 10-in-10 / 5-in-10 residential / combined, Meter Generator Output variants, EVSE residential/non-residential variants, PDR-LSR variants). SCME must submit net DER energy, DCR curtailment, the baseline used, and underlying hourly consumption for all baseline days. Any change to locations, capacity, baseline or SC requires a new UDC concurrence (Attachment A) submission
tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Sections 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6, 4.13.4; FERC Order 2222 Business Requirements Specification v1.2 (Jun 28 2024) BRQ-002, BRQ-005, BRQ-008, BRQ-009, BRQ-106; BPM for Demand Response Section 5 (baselines)
export_compensation: Net DER injection + DCR curtailment both settled at PNode LMP
stackable_with: Energy + Spin/Non-Spin as for DERA. Same double-counting guard as DERA: DER on a retail NEM program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred; UDC may raise double-counting concerns in its review

The only Order 2222 gate is the small-utility provision: CAISO may not accept a DERA containing customers of a utility that distributed 4 million MWh or less in the prior fiscal year unless that utility's RERRA permits it (DERP Agreement Appendix B.21 Section 4.1.4; the same opt-in already existed in the pro forma Demand Response Provider Agreement). In practice this reaches small California publicly owned utilities and MSS operators inside the CAISO BAA. Separately a DER on a retail net energy metering program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred from a DERA

incentive_structure: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LMP (at a proxy-generator PNode or GDF-weighted Sub-LAP aggregation) on Demand Response Energy Measurement = Customer Baseline minus actual load; paid only when bids clear at or above the monthly Net Benefits Test price threshold
incentive_value_usd: DMM-reported 2024 net energy market revenue per MWh delivered (RA-counted PDR): utility PDR about $144/MWh, third-party PDR about $48/MWh; per kW-year: utility PDR $1.59, third-party PDR $2.67 (2024), down from $26.97 and $15.18 (2022). Real-time soft offer cap $1,000/MWh (hard cap $2,000/MWh under stressed conditions); CPUC caps non-DRAM RA PDR bids at $949/MWh from 2024 (D.23-06-029)
event_limits: Minimum 100 kW curtailment for energy, sustainable for bid duration; must bid at or above the Net Benefits Test threshold price (Tariff 30.6.3, posted monthly); Day-Ahead and Real-Time energy; real-time bid dispatch option 60, 15 or 5 minutes (default 60; hourly-block option not eligible for energy bid cost recovery); all locations under one LSE and one Sub-LAP per registration (resource may span LSEs per comparison matrix); Demand Response Provider Agreement plus a certified SC; LSE and UDC 10-day location review in DRRS; outages only as 0 MW (all-or-nothing) PMax derates; telemetry not required for energy unless Pmax 10 MW or greater; statistical sampling permitted where interval metering is incomplete (min sample 271/(N+271)). Baselines: 10-in-10 (adj. cap 80-120%), 5-in-10 residential (71-140%), weather matching, control group (>=150 end users), Meter Generator Output (MGO) and combinations, EVSE

NEM locations may join, but any interval with net export at a location is set to zero under Customer Load Baseline methods; under MGO the storage/generator output counts only up to on-site demand and is zeroed while charging - so a PDR battery earns for offsetting on-site load, NOT for export. program_name: Proxy Demand Resource - Load Shift Resource (PDR-LSR)
incentive_structure: Two resource IDs: Curtailment (CUR) paid $/MWh LMP for load reduction/discharge like a PDR; Consumption (CON) bids from the bid floor up to below $0/MWh and is paid (negative LMP) for increasing load (charging) during oversupply
event_limits: Registered location(s) must include at least one behind-the-meter storage device (sub-metered). Must bid real-time in 5- or 15-minute intervals only (no hourly option); both IDs registered on the same GRDT with the same bid option, SC and effective dates. CUR ID: FUEL_TYPE GEN, eligible for RA and Spin/Non-Spin, must bid at or above the NBT threshold, non-export rules apply. CON ID: modeled like an NGR Dispatchable Demand Resource (MIN_GEN<0, MAX_GEN=0), ineligible for RA and ancillary services, bid must be below $0. Performance: storage-only configuration, or facility-load CLB plus storage (PDR-LSR with 5-in-10, 10-in-10, combined, or weather-matching)

export_compensation: No export credit - curtailment side uses non-export rules
stackable_with: The CUR side stacks with RA and Spin/Non-Spin; the CON side is energy-only. Charging credit only when the CON resource is dispatched at negative prices; ordinary retail-rate charging is not credited

Cannot offer Ancillary Services or RUC. Primarily utility Base Interruptible Program and agricultural pumping loads

No 2025+ DRAM deliveries. Reasons found: Nexant evaluation showed at most 3 of 6 criteria met; failed reliability and cost-competitiveness; bids at or near the CAISO price cap; demonstrated capacity 57% of contracted in 2021; 2024 solicitation offered only 73.05 MW vs 200+ MW/yr in 2018-2021

Customers remain free to be bid into CAISO as PDR by a third party - only the IOU-funded capacity contract ended

program_name: Resource Adequacy (RA) pathway for demand response - PDR/RDRR shown on LSE Supply Plans under the CPUC Slice-of-Day framework
incentive_structure: No CAISO capacity payment and no CAISO capacity auction. Value is a bilateral $/kW-month RA contract with a California LSE (IOU, CCA, ESP) or an IOU DR program (e.g. Capacity Bidding Program) that counts the PDR/RDRR toward the LSE's CPUC RA obligation
event_limits: CAISO side (BPM for Reliability Requirements Sections 7.1.1-7.1.2 as summarized in CAISO PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA matrix): System RA must-offer obligation - a PDR must bid whenever it has demand-reduction availability (24 h/day if capable); minimum DR MOO capability of 4 hours per dispatch, 3 consecutive days of dispatch, and 24 hours per month; PDR bids are not subject to local market power mitigation. Flexible RA: DR fits Use-Limited Super-Peak Ramping (MOO May-Sep 7am-12pm per matrix text, Oct-Apr 3-8pm; non-holiday weekdays; min 3 hours at EFC; at least 5 dispatches/month). CPUC side (2025 RA and Slice-of-Day Guide; D.23-04-010, D.23-06-029, D.24-06-004): DR shown for four consecutive hours of the Availability Assessment Hour window (or the full AAH window if contract/tariff requires longer dispatch); hourly value = capability on the worst day of the month under a 1-in-2 framework from ex ante Load Impact Protocol results; TLF and PRM adders removed, distribution loss factor adder retained; DR MCC bucket limit 8.3% of each slice; 17% PRM for 2025. Supply-side DR and storage may not be used to cover the LSE's storage-charging sufficiency requirement. RA NQC for DR must be re-authorized by the Local Regulatory Authority from the latest LIP before it is placed on CAISO's NQC list
tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 40 (RA), 40.10.3.2-40.10.3.4 (flexible categories); BPM for Reliability Requirements Sections 7.1.1, 7.1.2; CPUC D.23-04-010, D.23-06-029 (OP 29), D.24-06-004; CPUC 2025 RA and Slice of Day Filing Guide Section 7
stackable_with: RA-shown PDR and RDRR still earn CAISO energy (and PDR Spin/Non-Spin) revenues. The DERA/HDERA (DERP) model is INELIGIBLE to provide RA per the CAISO comparison matrix, so a BTM battery aggregation seeking RA value must register as PDR/PDR-LSR (CUR side only), not as a DERA. PDR-LSR Consumption ID is ineligible for RA. DRAM (IOU-funded RA contracts for third-party DR) ended Dec 31 2024

program_name: Ancillary Services (Regulation Up/Down, Spinning Reserve, Non-Spinning Reserve) - reachability for BTM aggregations and DMM clearing prices
incentive_structure: $/MW-hour capacity payment at the Day-Ahead ancillary service market clearing price; Real-Time pays only incremental capacity above the DA award; rescinded (No-Pay) if the resource does not perform
incentive_value_usd: DMM quantity-weighted average clearing prices ($/MW per hour), 2024 -> 2025. Day-Ahead: Reg Up $4.37 -> $3.40; Reg Down $6.29 -> $7.51; Spin $4.18 -> $0.84; Non-Spin $1.96 -> $0.94. Real-Time: Reg Up $7.18 -> $10.14; Reg Down $7.15 -> $16.18; Spin $1.03 -> $0.80; Non-Spin $0.85 -> $0.85. About 90% of 2025 AS cost was incurred day-ahead. Total CAISO AS cost $94.5M in 2025 ($0.47/MWh of load). DMM: actual CAISO batteries earned about $9/kW-yr from regulation in 2025; batteries supplied 53% of AS requirements
event_limits: Which BTM participation models can reach which product (CAISO PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA comparison matrix): PDR - Spin and Non-Spin only (500 kW minimum curtailment sustainable 30 min; direct telemetry at any size); DERA/HDERA - Energy plus Spin and Non-Spin (modeled as generic NGR, NON-REM subtype per Order 2222 BRS BRQ-002; direct telemetry required at any size for AS); REGULATION UP/DOWN is listed only for the Non-Generator Resource (NGR) model (LESR/DDR subtypes; 500 kW minimum; 4-second telemetry with 8-second round trip; 60-min continuous energy non-REM or 15-min under REM), which requires the ISO interconnection and New Resource Implementation process and ISO- or SC-metering of the resource - i.e. not a retail-meter BTM aggregation path. RDRR and the PDR-LSR Consumption ID cannot provide any AS. All AS requires AS certification (Tariff Appendix K) and unannounced compliance testing (7% of resources failed in 2025)
tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 8 and Appendix K (Ancillary Service Requirements Protocol); Tariff 4.17.7; BPM for Market Instruments Section 3.2; BPM for Direct Telemetry; DMM 2025 Annual Report on Market Issues and Performance Chapter 12 (Figures 12.4 and 12.5)
stackable_with: Co-optimized with energy for the same resource. BTM battery aggregations realistically reach Spin/Non-Spin (via PDR or DERA) but not Regulation; Regulation needs a wholesale-metered NGR. RA-shown PDR can also sell Spin/Non-Spin

program_name: WEIM / EDAM - access for customer-sited batteries in non-CAISO California balancing areas (LADWP, BANC/SMUD, TID, IID)
incentive_structure: No direct CAISO payment to the customer or a third-party aggregator. In WEIM, demand response enters only as a Load Forecast Adjustment submitted by the WEIM Entity (the utility/BA) - implicitly valued as a self-schedule; the BA, not the DR provider, sees any real-time imbalance settlement
event_limits: Answer: effectively NO direct path. The CAISO retail-DR and DER aggregation models (PDR, PDR-LSR, RDRR, DERA/HDERA) are CAISO-balancing-area participation models. In a WEIM BAA the only CAISO-recognized DR mechanism is the WEIM Entity's Load Forecast Adjustment (no minimum size; aggregated across forecast zones within the WEIM BAA; 5-minute schedule submitted a day ahead and updated to T-45; WEIM Entity must sign a DR attestation per EIM BPM Appendix C; no telemetry requirement). A BTM battery can only reach WEIM value indirectly through the host utility's own DR/VPP program. Status of the host BAs: TID has been a WEIM participant since 2021; LADWP and BANC (incl. SMUD) are WEIM participants and signed EDAM implementation agreements (BANC Nov 22 2024; LADWP Jan 13 2025) for planned EDAM entry in 2027; TID signed May 19 2025 for 2027; IID signed May 22 2025 for 2028. EDAM went live May 1 2026 with PacifiCorp (PGE planned 2026). CAISO matrix notes a day-ahead LFA option pending EDAM tariff approval
tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 29 (WEIM), 29.34 (WEIM Entity load forecast / DR); EDAM Tariff Section 33; BPM for Energy Imbalance Market Appendix C (Demand Response Attestation); EDAM Implementation Agreements for BANC, LADWP, TID, IID
stackable_with: Only via the POU's own retail program (e.g. SMUD, LADWP, TID DR/VPP programs), which is outside CAISO. FERC Order 2222 DER aggregation rights attach to RTO/ISO balancing areas and do not reach these public-power BAs
